newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - March 21.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - March 21.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Friday:

* On Thursday, the Dow Jones industrial average fell 57.40 points to 6,820.28 as blue-chip stocks tumbled after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan signalled that the central bank might raise interest rates next week.

* On Thursday, the minister for national development planning and head of the state planning board, Ginanjar Kartasasmita, said Indonesia's economy grew by 7.82 percent in calendar 1996, against a revised 8.21 percent in 1995.

* Bisnis Indonesia newspaper reported on Friday that the Finance Ministry had issued a decree requiring cigarette firms or importers to allocate 10 percent of their profits from retail sales for traders or suppliers. The allocation should be included in their cigarette retail prices.
The new decree also said retail prices would be set by the tax and excise directorate general, based on retail price calculations proposed by importers and cigarette makers.
* On Thursday, the Jakarta composite index closed 0.04 points lower at 663.13 points.
* On Friday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,405.40/05.90 at 0200 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,405.00/06.00
* Telkom after it announced slightly higher-than- expected net profits for 1996 of 1,503 billion rupiah, compared to a market expectation of 1,454 billion rupiah.
* Cigarette makers HM Sampoerna and Gudang Garam following the new government decree that cigarette companies should allocate 10 percent of profits from retail prices to traders and suppliers.
* Timber firm Barito Pacific on a report in Bisnis Indonesia that the government will give incentives to companies supplying timber to the domestic market.
* Trading firm Sekar Laut on market talk of a possible rights issue.
* Fishery firm Daya Guna Samudra on reports that President Suharto's son Bambang Trihatmodjo, who controls the Bimantara group, was likely to acquire a large stake in the firm.
* Transportation firm Mitra Rajasa on market talk that businessman Yopie Widjaja planned to acquire the firm. Widjadja has denied the rumour.
